text:
maria: quick bakeoff update — ran AWQ+GPTQ hybrid on llama3x-13b on the eval suite (squad/dev, winogrande, codegen-smoke). overall perplexity +0.8% vs fp16 but a few hallucination spikes on long-context prompts.

aj: can you point to where the deltas are coming from? per-layer breakdown?

maria: yes. instrumented per-layer KL and l2 drift. spikes localize to attn.q_proj layer 17 and ffn.g_proj layer 32, but it's mostly a tiny subset of channels in those layers (channels ~980-1030).

lee: hmm sounds like classic outlier channels. did you try simple channel clamp or per-channel scale?

maria: tried per-channel clamp at 3 sigma and it reduces hallucinations but increases token-level perplexity on code prompts. tradeoff not great.

toni: interesting — could be that clamp helps language but breaks distribution for code. did you check kv-cache behaviour (prefix caching)? sometimes clamping the qkv changes attention distribution over long histories.

maria: good point. reproducer: short prompt -> fine; long prompt (~1k tokens) -> hallucinations increase. suspect accumulation in KV cache from a handful of noisy channels.

aj: proposal: dynamic layer-skiplist autotune. autotuner runs a fast per-layer sensitivity scan (cheap evals) and builds a prioritized skiplist with per-tier budget. runtime will skip quantizing only the top-k sensitive channels per-request group based on prompt length.

lee: that could be nice — skipping at channel granularity instead of whole-layer skip reduces perf hit. what's the overhead?

aj: prototype runs in ~120s per model to build a baseline skiplist with a 5m eval budget. runtimes consult the skiplist plus a tiny heuristic (prompt_length > 512 -> include layer17 channels 990-1024).

maria: put a quick CLI together:
```
# run a fast sensitivity sweep
./skiplist_tuner --model ./weights/llama3x-13b --mode fast-sweep --budget 5m --metric ppl --out skiplist.json
# deploy with runtime flags
REDWOOD_SKIPLIST=skiplist.json REDWOOD_SKIP_MODE=dynamic ./serve --model llama3x-13b --quant awq+gptq
```

aj: sample tuner output (abbrev):
```
[00:12] layer=17 channel=1002 score=0.92
[00:12] layer=32 channel=981 score=0.88
[00:13] layer=17 channel=1019 score=0.81
summary: sensitive_channels=27 baseline_ppl=12.3
```

toni: curious what metric you're optimizing. default ppl might not catch hallucination collapse. maybe optimize a calibrated entailment score or QA F1 for SQuAD slices.

maria: started with ppl for speed but switched to a tiny QA pass for the top 5% most-sensitive channels. that caught hallucination cases better.

lee: what's the perf impact? skipping channels at runtime has branches; does it hurt throughput / batching?

aj: negligible if we implement skip as a mask in the matrix kernel (zero out quantized weights for selected channels) — single kernel path, same shape, so batching unaffected. the extra step is a tiny per-batch mask apply (~0.5–1% CPU).

maria: did A/B with 1000 requests: quality regressions down from 3.1%->0.7% while token throughput dropped 1.2%. cost delta acceptable.

toni: nice. we should also track regression alerts in Redwood Console: create per-model `sensitive_channel_policy` with auto-rollbacks if eval score drops >1.5x baseline.

lee: operational question — how do we persist skiplist across quant pipelines? e.g., if we re-quantize with AWQ tuning, indices shift?

aj: keep skiplist anchored to layer+channel index, and run a quick post-quant sanity sweep after any retrain/quant. the autotuner can be part of the quant pipeline: quant -> autotune -> validate -> package.

maria: found one oddity: channel indices that are sensitive at seq_len=256 are sometimes not at seq_len=1024. autotuner records context-length fingerprints and produces conditional rules. e.g., layer17:{990-1024} only active for seq>512.

toni: that's great — conditional skip rules will reduce unnecessary masking. can we add a small RL policy to trade off latency vs quality based on SLOs?

aj: possible, but let's keep simple heuristics first. RL adds complexity to rollback.

lee: sounds production-ready-ish. next steps: 1) add skiplist_tuner to infra CI, 2) add Console metric hooks (toni), 3) run cross-batch stability tests (maria/aj). I'll open a deploy PR. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: created PR #4789 for "dynamic skiplist autotune + runtime support" by lee — link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/p/r/4789

maria: thanks, leaving logs for the team in the experiment folder: gs://redwood-expts/quant/1951234567_dynamic_skip. I'll also dump the top-50 sensitive prompts for debugging.

aj: can you add a short reproducible notebook? one-click run will help SEs onboard.

maria: on it, will push a tiny colab-style notebook that runs the fast-sweep and shows before/after ppl + a tiny QA metric.

toni: awesome. capture the calibration set in the experiment metadata so we can re-eval in future runs.

lee: cool — let's roll the PR once CI green and the Console dashboards wired.

maria: thanks all. summary: dynamic channel-level skiplist autotune looks promising for long-context hallucinations with small perf tradeoffs. will iterate on heuristics and metrics. :rocket:
